svg.title: Test terminology map
svg.desc: Seven example tests aligned with tools, test sizes, the test pyramid, the Testing Trophy, and uses of common terms. Hatched bands mark examples whose classification varies by setup or source.
svg.text: Frontend and backend · a person checks the result
Exercise a flow in a remote environment
Frontend · complete a signed-in flow against the real API
Backend · exercise multiple services in a test environment
Frontend · exercise the UI with stubbed API responses
Backend · call the API with its database in a container
Run a real component or database
Frontend · interact with a component in a real browser
Backend · check interactions with a containerized database
Frontend · check component interactions in jsdom
Backend · connect a handler to a database test double
[1] A browser or database running on the same machine can fit Medium. A setup that communicates with other machines is Large. Small runs in one process without I/O or blocking calls.
[2] Dodds's examples treat a full app with stubbed HTTP responses as integration and a flow through the real backend as E2E. State what the system boundary includes.
The pyramid uses Google's example mix. The Trophy illustrates where to focus test effort. Start with the behavior you need to protect when placing an individual test.

[3] With Playwright, checking one component's public behavior can be a unit test. Checking collaboration can be integration. E2E through the real API can still fit Medium when everything runs on one machine.
[4] Vitest Browser Mode uses a real browser. Storybook stories can represent usage scenarios. Assign size based on the resources the setup allows.
[5] Testing Library works with the DOM in a simulated environment such as jsdom or in a real browser.
[6] go test and cargo test run tests of different scopes. A backend test with a local database container can fit Medium. Google gives server–database interaction as an integration example.
[7] Scenario tests use stories about how the system is used. Share the starting conditions, actions, expected result, and parts of the system exercised.
[8] ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1 lists functional testing as a test type. A test type can apply at one or several test levels. Google's book lists functional tests among the names for broad-scope tests.
Hatching marks examples whose classification varies by setup or source.
